jobs.title: Software Engineer
jobs.description:
India is the world's second-largest producer of fruits and vegetables, and loses over a lakh crore rupees of it every year between the farm and the shelf. Fresh Platter exists to fix that – not with an app, but by running the supply chain ourselves and engineering every step of it. We are hiring software engineers to build the brains of that system.

**About Fresh Platter**

Fresh Platter is a technology-driven fresh-produce supply-chain company, founded in Bengaluru in 2022. Every day we source from farms, then ripen, grade, pack and deliver fresh produce, using technology and data to improve quality, ensure consistent supply, minimise wastage and bring predictability to pricing. Around 100 people run the chain end to end, and the business is profitable.

We are also building our own machines and systems, because the bottlenecks we find in our operations cannot be fixed with software alone. Our harvest-handling rig cut bruising from around 30% to around 3%. Systems for farm selection, field scanning, produce movement and a fully automated packhouse are in build and design, with IISc and partner engineering firms. Five patent applications are filed.

Everything is built in three layers: a physical layer that moves and conditions produce, a sensing layer that reads its state, and an intelligence layer that decides what happens next and learns from the result. The crop changes. The architecture stays.

**The role**

We are building a high-quality software engineering team to own the sensing and intelligence layers, and the applications that run the business around them. You will join an existing team under our Tech Manager, and you will be expected to raise its bar, not just fill a seat.

We build with a new generation of AI-assisted development tools, seriously and every day. A small, sharp team here ships what used to need a large one. We will train you from your first week. If you already use these tools, good. If you have never touched one, that is fine – what we need is the raw ability to learn fast, think clearly and get things done.

**What you will build**

**Machines and sensing**

•   

The software that configures and controls our machines – reading their sensors, turning that data into decisions, and sending the right instructions back.

•   

The data path from sensor to screen: collection, storage, monitoring and alerts.

•   

Prototype-to-production work with our mechanical engineers, IISc and partner teams, tested on real machines in a real packhouse.

**Products and applications**

•   

The applications that run the chain: farm sourcing and procurement, ripening, grading and packing, inventory, logistics, quality and farm-to-customer traceability.

•   

Dashboards and alerts so teams see problems as they happen, not in next month's report.

•   

Integrations with the systems we already run – accounting, projects, mail and messaging – so data is captured once and flows wherever it is needed.

**AI-driven automation**

•   

Automation of the repetitive work across procurement, accounts and operations – checking purchase orders and vendor bills against their supporting documents, reconciliations, reporting and follow-ups.

•   

AI agents that read documents, emails and system records, decide what to do and act on it, with a person approving where it matters.

**Engineering practice**

•   

Own what you ship after it goes live – monitoring, fixes and improvements.

•   

Work across the stack: front end, back end, APIs, databases, device communication and data pipelines.

•   

Write tests, review code, deploy safely and document what you build.

•   

If you join with experience, help set the team's engineering standards and mentor the engineers who join after you.

**Who we are looking for**

•   

B.E. or B.Tech in Computer Science, Information Technology, Electronics and Communication, Electronics and Telecommunication, Electrical and Electronics, or a closely related engineering stream.

•   

0 to 4 years of experience. Freshers with a strong academic record and engineers who have shipped production software are both welcome. Title and responsibility will match experience.

•   

Solid programming fundamentals and problem-solving skills in at least one language.

•   

A working understanding of databases, web applications and APIs, and the ability to debug code you did not write.

•   

Someone who learns fast, goes deep rather than skimming, works around obstacles and stays steady when priorities change – humble enough to be trained from scratch, confident enough to question what does not make sense.

We're looking for a frontend developer with a designer's eye to build Sarvam's web experiences. You'll start with our marketing website: the homepage, product and use-case pages, interactive demos and calculators. You'll write production code, build reusable UI systems and turn rough ideas into polished interfaces, working closely with design, marketing and product engineering.
  
  
****Key Responsibilities****

* Build the interface, not just the mockup. Write production-ready Astro and React components with thoughtful layouts, typography and responsive behaviour. Own the implementation from first prototype to the final browser-sized detail.
* Build a UI system that holds together. Create reusable components, layout primitives and shared styles with clear APIs and sensible variants. Make the next page easier to build without turning every component into a 40-prop puzzle.
* Make it feel right. Build interactions, transitions and animations that make interfaces clearer and more enjoyable. Think through keyboard use, loading, empty and error states, reduced motion and what happens when the happy path isn't so happy.
* Prototype in code. Explore alternative layouts and interactions with designers, test ideas in the browser and refine the details together. You should be comfortable suggesting a better implementation, not waiting for every pixel and breakpoint to be specified.
* Build the useful bits properly. Develop interactive demos, calculators and forms; connect thm to APIs and content. Handle state, validation, asynchronous behaviour and failures. Keep accessibility, performance, metadata and measurement working as part of what you ship.
* Own the engineering quality. Make sound choices about component structure, rendering and hydration. Debug browser and performance issues, write appropriate tests, review code and check preview deployments. Ship maintainable changes that work beyond your own laptop.
* Astro, React, TypeScript and CSS are at the core of the work. We use GitHub for code review and Railway for development and pull-request previews. Sanity, ImageKit and PostHog support content, media and measurement. You'll work with engineering on staging and production releases.

****Requirements****

* Have built and shipped interfaces you're proud to put your name on. Show us the actual thing, what you coded and the decisions you made. A live link beats a paragraph of adjectives.
* Have strong HTML, CSS, JavaScript and TypeScript fundamentals and hands-on React experience. You can work effectively in Astro and reason about component composition, state, rendering and browser behaviour.
* Have a good eye for visual design and the CSS skills to act on it. You care about spacing, type, hierarchy, responsive layouts and interaction details, and can turn that judgement into working code.
* Can work across design and engineering. You're comfortable starting from a rough brief, prototyping options and discussing trade-offs with designers. You can also take an established design and implement it faithfully.
* Can debug an unfamiliar frontend, integrate APIs and use Git, pull requests and automated checks confidently. You understand accessibility and web performance, and handle credentials and user data responsibly.
* Use AI coding tools with judgement. Let them help you move faster. Read the diff, test the result and be able to explain what you're shipping. 'The model wrote it' isn't a debugging strategy.
* Ask good questions when the brief is fuzzy. Explain trade-offs, suggest a practical way forward and use evidence before declaring that something needs fixing.

****Bonus points that are not dealbreakers****

* You've built for B2B SaaS, developer tools or AI products.
* You've built component libraries, design systems or interactive prototypes that other people actually use.
* You've worked with animation, SVG, Canvas or other techniques that make complex ideas easier to explore on the web.
* You've used a headless CMS such as Sanity, or worked on technical SEO and analytics integrations without letting them take over the frontend.

****How to apply****
Skip the generic cover letter. Send us a couple of interfaces or web projects you've built, with a short note on what you personally designed and coded. Pick one and walk us through a component, interaction or tricky engineering decision. Code samples are welcome where you can share them.
  
  
If there's a side project you're weirdly proud of, we'd like to see that too.
  
  
****Why Sarvam?****
Sarvam is a fast-moving, high talent-density team building full-stack AI for India, working on problems that push the frontiers of AI with real population-scale impact.
  
  

* Work alongside researchers, engineers, builders, and business leaders who move fast and hold each other to a very high bar
* High ownership and high impact, from day one
* Everything we do is AI-first, from the way we build and ship to the way we think about problems
* You can work on problems that could change how an entire country learns, works, and communicates

If you want to work on problems at the frontier of AI in India, Sarvam is the place to be.

**Job Description or Responsibilities**

***Flow development in OO Studio***

* Design, build, and maintain flows and subflows in OO Studio (and OO Workflow Designer where used), covering inputs, outputs, results, transitions, and responses.
* Develop custom operations using Java, Python/Jython, PowerShell, SSH, SQL, and HTTP/REST operations.
* Build reusable flows and operations, and apply consistent naming, structure, and versioning standards.
* Configure system accounts, system properties, selection lists, and configuration items securely, avoiding hard-coded credentials and environment values.
* Build robust error handling, retries, timeouts, and logging into flows so failures are clear and recoverable.
* Automate IT processes such as user provisioning, server and cloud operations, patching, monitoring remediation, and service request fulfillment.

***Content packs***

* Develop, package, and version custom content packs, and manage dependencies on OpenText base and integration content packs.
* Upgrade out-of-the-box content packs, test impact, and fix broken flows after upgrades.
* Promote content packs across dev, test, and production through OO Central, following the team's release and change process.
* Manage content in source control (Git/SVN with OO Studio SCM integration).

***Integrations***

* Build integrations between OO and enterprise systems, such as ServiceNow, Active Directory/Entra ID, VMware, monitoring tools, databases, and ticketing systems.
* Build and consume REST/SOAP APIs, including authentication (OAuth 2.0, basic auth, API keys, certificates).
* Configure and maintain Remote Action Servers (RAS) and worker groups for executing operations across network zones.
* Support triggers from other systems, for example SMAX processes, monitoring alerts, or schedules, and make sure results flow back correctly.

***Full-stack development***

* Develop backend services and scripts (Java, Python, PowerShell) that support automation.
* Build or maintain simple web front ends, APIs, or dashboards that start or report on automations where needed.
* Work with databases (SQL Server, Oracle, PostgreSQL) for OO data, reporting, and integration logic.

***Operations (run)***

* Monitor flow runs, schedules, RAS health, and OO Central, and act on failures before users are affected.
* Troubleshoot failed or stuck runs using run logs, debugger, and step-level details.
* Resolve L2/L3 incidents for the automations the team owns, within SLA, and turn permanent fixes into backlog items.
* Take part in the team's on-call or support rotation.
* Support OO platform upgrades, patches, and certificate renewals together with platform administrators.
* Maintain runbooks, flow documentation (purpose, inputs, dependencies, owners), and known-error records.

***Migration support***

* Document existing OO flows and integrations clearly, so the ServiceNow team can assess and rebuild them in Workflow Studio and IntegrationHub.
* Work with ServiceNow developers during migration waves, explaining flow logic, dependencies, and edge cases, and supporting side-by-side testing and cutover.

**Position Name:** Middleware Developer (C&C++) — ADAS

**Years of Experience:** 3- 7 years

**Location:** Bengaluru, Karnataka

#### 

#### **About Vayavya Labs**

Vayavya Labs builds embedded software and firmware for the semiconductor and automotive industries, with deep expertise in low-level device software, driver automation, and safety-critical systems. Our engineers work close to the metal — bringing up silicon, writing production firmware, and validating it to the standards demanded by modern and autonomous vehicles. We are expanding our middleware and platform-software capability to support the next generation of software-defined vehicles, where robust, well-architected middleware is what connects hardware to the applications that run on it.

#### 

#### **About the Role**

We are looking for a C/C++ Middleware Developer to design, implement, and maintain the middleware layer of a vehicle compute platform built for ADAS and autonomous driving. This is the layer where inter-process communication frameworks, service daemons, hardware abstraction interfaces, and system services come together to carry sensor data and control signals between low-level drivers and the autonomy software that depends on them. You will work within and contribute to the team’s in-house C++ middleware frameworks — not building from scratch in isolation, but extending, hardening, and optimizing a shared codebase that other engineers build on.

The role combines strong C++ systems programming with an understanding of how embedded software stacks are organized — from device drivers through middleware services to application interfaces. You will collaborate closely with firmware engineers, driver developers, perception and planning teams, and will be expected to write production-quality, testable, well-documented code that runs in resource-constrained, safety-adjacent environments. You should be comfortable working in a large, shared C++ codebase with established patterns, contributing clean code that other engineers review, extend, and rely on.

#### 

#### **What You’ll Do**

* Design and implement middleware components in C++ (C++14/17) that provide well-defined interfaces between platform services, device drivers, and application software.
* Develop and maintain inter-process communication (IPC) frameworks — D-Bus like services, shared-memory interfaces, zero-copy transports (e.g. Eclipse iceoryx), POSIX message queues, and Unix domain sockets — for reliable, low-latency communication between system daemons, sensor pipelines, and application software.
* Implement system services and background daemons on embedded Linux — managing lifecycle, configuration, logging, health monitoring, and error recovery.
* Write and integrate hardware abstraction layers (HALs) that expose sensor data, actuator controls, and peripheral status to higher-level software through clean, versioned APIs.
* Develop middleware for vehicle communication stacks — receiving and routing CAN, Ethernet, or serial data from the platform’s networking layer and exposing it to application consumers as structured service interfaces.
* Build and maintain configuration management, parameter storage, and runtime-tunable settings frameworks for embedded platforms.
* Work within and contribute to the team’s in-house C++ middleware frameworks — understanding the existing architecture, following established coding patterns and API conventions, and extending the framework with new modules as the platform evolves.
* Integrate third-party and silicon-vendor SDKs into the middleware stack — wrapping vendor libraries behind clean, testable C++ interfaces that isolate the rest of the platform from vendor-specific APIs and versioning.
* Develop middleware components for sensor data routing — receiving high-bandwidth data from camera, lidar, and radar interfaces and delivering it to perception and fusion consumers through well-defined, latency-aware service interfaces.
* Implement platform health monitoring and diagnostics services — collecting hardware status, software health metrics, and error conditions from across the middleware stack and exposing them for logging, alerting, and fleet-level telemetry.
* Profile and optimize middleware for CPU usage, memory footprint, latency, and thread safety using tools such as perf, Valgrind, strace, and GDB.
* Write unit tests (Google Test / Google Mock), integration tests, and system-level tests for middleware components, and integrate them into CI/CD pipelines.
* Collaborate with firmware engineers on bring-up and integration — understanding how middleware depends on driver and BSP behavior, and debugging issues that span the middleware-driver boundary.
* Participate in architecture and design reviews, contribute to coding standards, and maintain clear technical documentation for middleware APIs and service interfaces.

#### **What You’ll Bring**

* 3–7 years of hands-on C/C++ software development experience, with at least 2 years focused on middleware, platform services, or system-level software.
* Strong modern C++ skills (C++14 or later) — comfortable with RAII, smart pointers, move semantics, STL containers and algorithms, templates, and lambda expressions in production code.
* Solid understanding of Linux system programming — processes, threads (pthreads / std::thread), synchronization primitives (mutexes, condition variables, semaphores), signals, file descriptors, epoll/select, and the POSIX API.
* Experience designing and implementing IPC mechanisms — at least one of: D-Bus (sd-bus or GDBus), shared memory, POSIX message queues, Unix domain sockets, or named pipes — in a multi-process embedded or systems-software context.
* Working knowledge of the Linux build and packaging ecosystem — CMake (and ideally colcon for ROS 2 workspaces) for build, pkg-config for dependency management, and familiarity with cross-compilation toolchains for ARM targets.
* Comfortable with debugging and profiling tools — GDB, Valgri
